newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open steady to firm.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open steady to firm Thursday, with gold and silver still consolidating after hitting multi-year lows earlier this month, while platinum-group metals saw further gains on TOCOM overnight.
COMEX December gold was called unchanged to up $0.20 from Wednesday's close of $330.60 an ounce.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $326.35/65 early against the London morning fix of $326.00 and Wednesday's New York close at $325.80/$326.30.
Overnight, the central bank of Lithuania said it was considering following the lead of other European central banks by selling some of its gold reserves in the future, though not this year.
But Lithuania only held total gold and foreign currency reserves valued at $939.60 million at the end of June, of which $62.1 million was gold.
COMEX September silver was called unchanged to up 0.3 cent from Wednesday's close of $4.373.
COMEX silver stocks fell a further 928,598 ounces to 170,900,958 ounces, a new low since the addition of Wilmington Trust stocks in January. COMEX gold stocks declined 5,653 ounces to 914,075 ounces.
NYMEX October platinum and September palladium were called steady to up $1.00 from the previous closes of $424.40 and $198.00, respectively.
Platinum-group futures surged even higher on TOCOM overnight as shortcovering continued, with spot market sales of PGMs by Russia not meeting pent-up demand, traders said.
